claims.statement: LLMProvider in summary/llm_client.rs defines seven variants (OpenAI, Claude, Groq, Ollama, OpenRouter, BuiltInAI, CustomOpenAI); from_str is case-insensitive, accepts aliases 'builtin-ai'/'local-llama'/'localllama' for BuiltInAI and 'custom-openai' for CustomOpenAI, and returns Err for anything else.

generate_summary routes BuiltInAI to summary_engine::generate_with_builtin with an early return before any endpoint selection, so BuiltInAI never issues HTTP; all other providers resolve to an HTTP URL in the same function (fixed cloud URLs for OpenAI/Groq/OpenRouter/Claude, {ollamaEndpoint}/v1/chat/completions for Ollama defaulting to http://localhost:11434, {endpoint}/chat/completions for CustomOpenAI).

Claude uses a dedicated request shape in llm_client: system prompt in a top-level 'system' field, only a user message in messages, hardcoded max_tokens 2048, x-api-key and anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 headers instead of a Bearer token, and responses parsed as content[0].text rather than choices[0].message.content.

Non-Claude HTTP providers serialize a two-message ChatRequest (system + user) with max_tokens/temperature/top_p omitted when None; only CustomOpenAI forwards caller-supplied sampling parameters — for OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, and Ollama the three fields are always None.

Every LLM HTTP request uses a 300-second request timeout and is raced against the meeting's CancellationToken via tokio::select!, returning 'Summary generation was cancelled' when the token fires; on a reqwest timeout the error message string still says 'timed out after 60 seconds' despite the 300 s constant.

API keys are stored per provider in dedicated columns of the singleton settings row (id='1'): openaiApiKey, anthropicApiKey, groqApiKey, openRouterApiKey, and ollamaApiKey, mapped by string provider name in SettingsRepository::save_api_key/get_api_key/delete_api_key; builtin-ai requires no key and custom-openai is rejected as a column-backed provider.

api_save_model_config upserts the provider/model/whisperModel/ollamaEndpoint row, writes a non-empty API key to the provider-mapped column unless the provider is custom-openai, and then triggers summary_engine::shutdown_sidecar_gracefully so switching provider or model tears down a running BuiltInAI sidecar without blocking the UI; api_get_api_key returns the stored key for a provider or an empty string.

The custom-openai provider keeps endpoint, apiKey, model, maxTokens, temperature, and topP as one CustomOpenAIConfig JSON document in the settings.customOpenAIConfig column; save_api_key refuses it, get_api_key('custom-openai') extracts apiKey from the parsed JSON, and delete_api_key nulls the whole column.

api_save_custom_openai_config validates the endpoint (http:// or https://, non-empty), model (non-empty), temperature in 0.0-2.0, top_p in 0.0-1.0, max_tokens >= 1, and filters blank API keys before serializing the config into the settings row.

api_test_custom_openai_connection posts a minimal chat completion ('Hi', max_tokens 5, 30 s timeout, Bearer auth only when a key is present) to {endpoint}/chat/completions and reports success only when the 200 response contains choices[0] with a message.content or message.reasoning_content field; a 200 that is not OpenAI-shaped or is invalid JSON is an error.

The key-bearing model-discovery commands get_openai_models, get_anthropic_models, and get_groq_models share a template: no/blank key returns a hardcoded fallback list immediately; otherwise a per-crate global MODELS_CACHE with a 300-second TTL is consulted, the API is fetched with a 5-second timeout, results are filtered to chat-capable models, and any failure (transport, HTTP status, parse, or empty result) degrades to the fallback list instead of an error.

Chat-model filters differ per provider: OpenAI keeps gpt-*/o1-*/o3-*/o4-*/chatgpt-* while excluding embedding, tts, whisper, dall-e, babbage, davinci, instruct, realtime, and audio ids; Groq excludes ids containing whisper, embed, guard, or tool-use; Anthropic keeps only ids starting with 'claude-'.

get_openrouter_models is the outlier discovery command: it is a synchronous command using a blocking reqwest client, requires no API key because OpenRouter's catalog is public, applies no cache, returns richer per-model data (name, context_length preferring top_provider.context_length, prompt/completion pricing), and propagates errors instead of falling back.

get_ollama_models validates the endpoint scheme, wraps discovery in a 5-second timeout, GETs {endpoint}/api/tags with up to 2 retries and exponential backoff (300 ms initial, aborting on invalid-endpoint/404 errors), and falls back to executing 'ollama list' and parsing its table output only when the endpoint is localhost/empty; an empty model list is a NoModelsFound error, not an empty result.

pull_ollama_model streams /api/pull (NDJSON, 10-minute timeout) and emits ollama-model-download-progress, ollama-model-download-error, and ollama-model-download-complete Tauri events; a global DOWNLOADING_MODELS set rejects duplicate downloads and is cleaned up on every exit path. delete_ollama_model issues DELETE /api/delete with a 30-second timeout.

ModelMetadataCache (ollama/metadata.rs) caches model metadata keyed by '{model}::{endpoint}' with a 300-second TTL; two independent global instances exist — one in ollama.rs behind get_ollama_model_context and one in summary/service.rs for chunk planning.

Ollama context-size resolution cascades: model_info context keys from /api/show (verbose), then regex 'PARAMETER num_ctx' in the modelfile, then a hardcoded family table (llama 4096, mistral/qwen/gemma 8192, codellama/deepseek 16384, phi 2048, neural-chat 4096); get_ollama_model_context returns 4000 on any fetch failure rather than an error.

SummaryService::process_transcript_background skips key retrieval for Ollama/BuiltInAI/CustomOpenAI (empty string) and requires a stored key for every other provider, failing the run with 'API key not found for {provider}' otherwise; CustomOpenAI's key is replaced by the apiKey from its JSON config, and its endpoint comes from that config — a missing config fails the run.

Token thresholds are provider-specific: Ollama uses metadata-cache context_size minus 300 (fallback 4000), BuiltInAI uses its model registry context_size minus 300 (fallback 1748 for unknown models), and cloud providers including CustomOpenAI get 100000, which makes generate_meeting_summary take the single-pass path for all cloud providers regardless of transcript length.

generate_meeting_summary chooses single-pass when the provider is not Ollama/BuiltInAI or the transcript is under the token threshold; otherwise it chunks (threshold minus 300 tokens, 100-token overlap), summarizes each chunk sequentially with a cancellation check before each, combines multiple chunk summaries joined by '---', and renders the final template report — cancellation is re-checked before the final pass.

Cancellation is per-meeting via a global CANCELLATION_REGISTRY of meeting_id to CancellationToken; api_cancel_summary cancels the token and marks the row cancelled, and because error classification in the service matches errors containing the substring 'cancelled', the cancellation message text in llm_client/processor is the contract that keeps rows 'cancelled' rather than 'failed'.

generate_with_builtin resolves the model from a hardcoded GGUF catalog (qwen3.5:2b, qwen3.5:4b, gemma3:4b, gemma3:1b, all 32768-token contexts under app_data_dir/models/summary), formats the prompt with the model's chat template, ensures the llama-helper sidecar is running, and sends a JSON generate request with DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=4096 and a 900-second timeout raced against the cancellation token — cancelling shuts the sidecar down.

Fresh installs default to BuiltInAI: initialize_fresh_database writes provider 'builtin-ai' with the RAM-based recommendation (qwen3.5:4b for >= 14 GB RAM, else qwen3.5:2b), keeping summary generation fully local out of the box.

api_process_transcript records the provider string in transcript_chunks, resets the summary_processes row, spawns process_transcript_background, and returns a process_id before any LLM traffic; all provider calls happen in the background task and results/errors/status are read back from summary_processes via api_get_summary polling.

The settings table grew by migration: the initial schema created groq/openai/anthropic/ollama key columns, then openRouterApiKey (20250920155811), ollamaEndpoint (20251010153942), and customOpenAIConfig (20251105120000) were added; migration 20251229000000 also adds geminiApiKey, but no Gemini variant exists in LLMProvider, SettingsRepository, or the frontend provider union, making it dead schema.

The frontend never calls LLM APIs directly: ModelSettingsModal treats only claude/groq/openai/openrouter as requiring an API key, fills model pickers from the per-provider discovery commands (with frontend hardcoded fallback lists for OpenAI/Claude/Groq when the fetch returns empty), caches Ollama models per endpoint in-component, and for custom-openai saves the JSON config first and uses the typed model name as the model field.

The webview CSP connect-src allowlist in tauri.conf.json is 'self', http://localhost:11434 (Ollama default port), http://localhost:5167 (hardcoded legacy backend URL), http://localhost:8178 (archived whisper-server), and https://api.ollama.ai; all LLM chat traffic is issued by the Rust core via reqwest, so the allowlist governs webview-side requests rather than the summary path.

api_get_model_config returns the settings row as ModelConfig with the API key resolved for the row's provider (from the customOpenAIConfig JSON for custom-openai); the frontend fetches keys on demand via api_get_api_key when the config row omits them, and ConfigContext prefetches the claude/groq/openai/openrouter keys on mount.
